transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Avery (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Emilia Torres (Redwood Solutions), Michael Chen (Silverpine CISO), Leah Ortiz (Silverpine Dir Eng), Samir Patel (Silverpine Sec Eng), Rita Gomez (Silverpine Compliance)

Summary:
Quick posture review for SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 evidence needs. Walkthrough of Trust Center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO, audit logs forwarding, KMS/encryption, and data residency options. Agreed next steps to share reports and map controls; schedule technical follow-up for SIEM/logging integration.

Topics: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO27001 certificate, Trust Center read-only access, controls mapping spreadsheet, RBAC and SSO (Okta/SAML), audit log retention and forwarding, encryption at rest (KMS/HSM), data residency (EU region), private deployment options (VPC/dedicated).

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec, uh, this is Jordan from Redwood. You all good on audio?
[00:08] Michael: Yep, good here. Thanks for organizing.
[00:12] Priya: Hi team, Priya here, I'll drive the technical portions, happy to go over the controls mapping and the infra questions.
[00:18] Leah: Thanks. Rita and Samir are on as well, just listening in for compliance and infra.
[00:22] Rita: hi
[00:25] Jordan: Cool, objective today is a posture review - SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 - show what artifacts we can share, how to map controls, and answer any questions about logging/keys/residency.
[00:33] Michael: Perfect. Our timeline: looking to finish vendor assessments by end of May, want to know if Redwood meets our encryption and log forwarding needs.
[00:39] Priya: Great. Quick note - apologies in advance, transcription sometimes shows Redwood Dedicate instead of Redwood Dedicated, so ignore typos.
[00:45] Samir: ha, noted.
[00:47] Priya: Ok, I'll start with what we can provide today: SOC 2 Type II report redacted for customer info, ISO27001 certificate, and a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps our controls to common frameworks and show where evidence lives. We can also give read-only Trust Center access for reviewers.
[01:03] Michael: When you say Trust Center, is that a portal where we can see audit logs and certs, or is it just the documents?
[01:09] Jordan: It's a portal; the Trust Center contains certificates, compliance docs, controls mapping, and some admin-level docs. We can provision read-only view (no admin access) for your auditors. Link: https://trust.redwood-inference.example.com (we'll share proper link in follow-up).
[01:22] Rita: Are there any NDAs needed before we share the Type II report? We have vendor policy about sensitive documents.
[01:27] Jordan: Good question - we can share under a standard NDA, but most customers request the report under an MSA or an NDA. I'll include the PDF as a secured share and note the access permissions.
[01:35] Leah: On controls mapping, can you show an example of how you map a control to evidence? e.g., encryption key rotation evidence.
[01:42] Priya: Sure - in the spreadsheet we have a column for control ID, description, responsible owner, where evidence is stored (S3 path or Trust Center doc), and sample evidence snapshot. For KMS rotation we'll point to our KMS audit log entries and an ops runbook.
[01:55] Samir: Which KMS do you use? Is that cloud provider KMS or a Redwood-managed HSM?
[02:01] Priya: Currently we integrate with cloud KMS providers for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private we offer customer-managed KMS options and HSM integrations on request. We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own-key via customer HSM in Private deployments.
[02:16] Michael: So if we need a full HSM-backed key under our tenancy, is that possible for a VPC/private deployment?
[02:22] Priya: Yes, for Private we can support customer-managed keys with HSM, though that requires an initial onboarding and ops playbook. We'll document the steps in the controls mapping.
[02:31] Jordan: Also to highlight, encryption in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3, at rest uses AES-256 and KMS for key management.
[02:38] Rita: What about RBAC and SSO? We use Okta and SCIM provisioning.
[02:43] Priya: We offer SSO via SAML and OIDC, SCIM provisioning for user sync, and role-based access control in the Console. We can map SSO provisioning evidence and SCIM logs as part of identity controls.
[02:53] Leah: Are there audit logs that show user actions, admin changes, and things like key creation? What's the retention?
[02:59] Priya: Audit logs capture admin actions, model deployments, config changes, and API-level events. Default retention for hosted is 90 days; we can support longer retention as an add-on or via log forwarding to your SIEM. For Dedicated/Private retention policies can be configured.
[03:14] Samir: Log forwarding — do you support syslog/S3/Kinesis or only API pulls? We want to ingest into Splunk/Sumo/Datadog.
[03:20] Priya: We support pushing to S3 buckets, streaming with Kinesis or PubSub, and HTTP webhooks for log delivery; common pattern is push to a customer-owned S3 or Kinesis then your SIEM pulls from there. We'll include recommended patterns in the technical follow-up.
[03:33] Michael: Any PII in logs? We need assurance logs are redacted or stored appropriately.
[03:38] Priya: Logs are event metadata; we avoid storing message-level PII for hosted customers. For workloads where user content must be retained, we have options to enable data residency and retention controls; those will be called out in the controls mapping and Trust Center.
[03:51] Jordan: Quick interruption — a note on transcription: sometimes company names get mangled, excuse the typos.
[03:56] Rita: no worries
[03:58] Priya: Back to encryption keys — rotation schedule is typically 90 days for data keys and customer-managed key rotation cadence is agreed during onboarding. Evidence: rotation logs from KMS, change requests, and signed runbooks.
[04:12] Leah: For ISO27001, do you provide Annex A mappings or just certificate and scope?
[04:17] Priya: We provide the ISO27001 certificate plus an Annex-level mapping for the controls we cover versus responsibilities retained by customers. The mapping shows which controls Redwood owns, which are shared, and which are customer responsibilities.
[04:29] Samir: On shared controls, can you show an example — say patch management for the OS?
[04:33] Priya: Sure — for hosted Redwood manages patching at the infra layer; for Private we provide the process and recommend customer-run patching in air-gapped setups. We'll include CVE tracking and patch evidence references.
[04:46] Michael: What about penetration testing and vuln scans? Do you share results?
[04:50] Jordan: We share summary reports for vuln scanning and can provide high-level PT reports with redactions; for detailed PT results we typically require an NDA.
[04:58] Rita: Do you have SOC 2 Type II coverage for data centers in EU? Our vendor risk team needs region-specific coverage.
[05:05] Priya: Our SOC 2 Type II covers the control scope regardless of region for the control environment, but for data residency we can point to region-specific deployments and addendum in the Trust Center. We'll call out which controls apply to EU-hosted instances.
[05:18] Leah: How do you handle data residency for model inference if we need EU-only?
[05:22] Priya: You can choose an EU-hosted region for Redwood Hosted; for Dedicated/Private you can deploy on customer-controlled infra or in the EU region to meet residency requirements. We'll include deployment architecture diagrams in follow-up.
[05:36] Samir: Ok, question about audit log tamper-proofing — are logs write-once or are they changeable?
[05:41] Priya: We implement immutability patterns for audit logs: write-once S3 buckets with object lock when requested, and we maintain checksums/timestamps. For high-assurance customers we recommend forwarding to your SIEM with independent retention.
[05:54] Michael: For compliance reviewers, will you provide a mapping that shows exactly which artifact proves each control?
[05:59] Priya: Yes, that's the controls mapping spreadsheet — each control maps to artifact name, location in Trust Center or S3, and sample evidence. We'll attach screenshots where allowed.
[06:10] Jordan: We'll also include a guidance doc for evidence collection to make your audit team's job easier.
[06:15] Rita: On SSO, if we use SCIM to auto-provision, can we enforce RBAC roles from Okta groups?
[06:21] Priya: Yes, we map Okta groups to Console roles; SCIM syncing handles membership and you can define role mappings. Evidence: SCIM provisioning logs and role mapping snapshot.
[06:31] Leah: Are there any known gaps in your current controls that we should be aware of?
[06:35] Priya: Nothing material for the control scope we cover; a common gap is customer-side processes — e.g., customer key rotation policies or endpoint security — which we'll flag as shared responsibilities in the mapping.
[06:47] Samir: How long does it take to get Trust Center read-only access set up for an auditor?
[06:52] Jordan: Usually under 48 hours once we have the user list and their emails; we do an ID verification step for external auditors.
[06:58] Michael: Can we get machine-readable evidence for automation? Our toolkit ingests JSON/CSV.
[07:03] Priya: We can provide exports — the mapping spreadsheet and certain logs can be exported as CSV/JSON. Some artifacts are PDFs but we add metadata for automation.
[07:12] Leah: Let's talk about legal and procurement - do you provide standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA) that includes data residency clauses?
[07:18] Jordan: Yes, DPA with standard EU SCCs if needed, and we have addenda for residency requirements. Procurement usually signs the DPA + MSA.
[07:25] Rita: For background checks or personnel security, is there any summary we can include?
[07:30] Priya: We provide background check policy summaries (levels of checks for on-prem staff vs contractors) and org chart for control owners. We'll redacted personal details.
[07:40] Samir: A bit more on logs — what fields are included in an API audit event? Requester ID, IP, resource, action?
[07:45] Priya: Yes: timestamp, requester ID, request IP, resource path, action, response status, and correlation ID. No full content is included unless configured.
[07:55] Michael: About certification dates — when was the last SOC 2 audit performed?
[07:59] Jordan: Last Type II period ended March 31, 2026, report issued April 2026. We'll share the PDF.
[08:06] Leah: Good. For ISO27001 what's the scope? Production infra and control plane?
[08:11] Priya: Scope covers the control plane, production infra, and hosted service operations. We'll include scope docs and mapping.
[08:20] Samir: For dedicated capacity, do you provide separate logs per tenant? We need per-tenant separation for audit evidence.
[08:26] Priya: Yes, Dedicated provides tenant-level logs and isolation. We'll include how to pull per-tenant evidence in follow-up.
[08:34] Jordan: We are at about 8 minutes in — just making timestamps for the transcript, will keep going.
[08:39] Rita: This is helpful.
[08:41] Priya: On incident response and forensics — we have an IR plan, runbooks, and we've had tabletop exercises; summary can be shared as redacted. We also provide notification SLA commitments in enterprise contracts.
[08:55] Michael: Do you have SOC 2 controls around vendor management / subprocessor controls?
[09:00] Priya: Yes, vendor management controls exist and we maintain a subprocessor list in the Trust Center. We'll include a copy of the subprocessor roster.
[09:07] Leah: For legal, retention, and e-discovery, any support to pull historical logs for legal holds?
[09:12] Priya: Yes, for customers with longer-term retention we can assist with exports and e-discovery pulls — usually an on-call ops request and we provide packaged evidence.
[09:22] Samir: A quick nit: does Redwood do red-team testing?
[09:26] Priya: We do internal red-team and coordinate external pentests annually; summary high-level findings are in Trust Center.
[09:33] Jordan: Ok, shifting to concrete next steps — Jordan will share SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, Priya will share controls mapping and technical doc, schedule tech follow-up.
[09:42] Michael: We'll send a list of required artefacts and auditor emails for Trust Center access.
[09:47] Rita: Also need a copy of the DPA and SCCs.
[09:50] Jordan: We'll include DPA + SCCs in the share.
[09:54] Priya: Any other technical blockers?
[09:56] Leah: Not yet, but we'll validate SIEM ingestion patterns with Samir in the follow-up.
[10:01] Samir: Sounds good.
[10:03] Priya: One more thing on evidence — for some controls we will provide screenshots with timestamps; for others it's log extracts. We'll mark sensitive items as redacted.
[10:14] Jordan: I'll confirm NDA requirements in the follow-up before we attach the Type II report.
[10:18] Michael: That's fine.
[10:20] Jordan: Great. Recap of action items... (see action_items list). We'll aim to get docs over within 48 hours.
[10:29] Rita: Appreciate it.
[10:31] Michael: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:33] Jordan: Thanks everyone, bye.
[10:35] End of meeting

Notes/Links to share: Trust Center link (to be provided in follow-up), controls mapping spreadsheet (CSV/Google Sheet), SOC 2 Type II PDF (secure share), ISO27001 cert (PDF), DPA + SCCs (PDF).

Transcript notes: Slight transcription errors present (e.g., Redwood Dedicate -> Redwood Dedicated), speaker labels approximate.
